interest: This document provides valuable insight into the postwar intersection of private American commercial interests and U.S. government policy regarding Japanese industrial and intellectual property rights. It illustrates how the National Foreign Trade Council actively sought wartime Japanese legislation (the 1917 and 1943 laws) from the State Department during the Allied Occupation to evaluate the status of foreign patents, trademarks, and prewar commercial assets. The accompanying charge-out sheet also illuminates the archival life cycle of these records, showing sustained diplomatic and legal research into Tokyo despatches and Far Eastern Commission files into the early 1960s.
overview: This file from the Department of State central decimal file 894.541 relates to Japanese industrial and intellectual property during and following World War II. It comprises an October 13, 1948 letter from Raymond Vernon, Assistant Chief of the International Resources Division, transmitting English translations of the Japanese Wartime Laws of Industrial Property of 1917 and 1943 to W.E.F. Bradley of the National Foreign Trade Council, following an earlier conference. The file also includes a later State Department charge-out form (Form DS-1033) recording the loan of related Tokyo despatches, Far Eastern Commission materials, and decimal files to departmental personnel in 1960 and 1962.

subfiles.from: Raymond Vernon, Assistant Chief, International Resources Division
subfiles.summary: Raymond Vernon writes to W.E.F. Bradley of the National Foreign Trade Council to transmit copies of the Japanese Wartime Laws of Industrial Property of 1917 and 1943, fulfilling a request made to Mr. Dixon during a September 24 conference. Vernon notes that transmission was delayed to verify the authenticity of the copies and remarks that although the translations leave something to be desired, their meaning is clear. The enclosed texts comprise the War-Time Law of Industrial Property and the War-Time Special Regulations of Industrial Property Law.

The records were charged out to Stauffer (PHO) on May 18, 1960, and to Mr. Shippe (47E) on June 26, 1962, by records clerk Jovino.
